tagline: A home pizza guide and dough calculator

footer.disclaimer: Amounts and times are approximate; change one thing at a time.

home.title: Home pizza guide
home.pitch: Six pizza styles for a home oven that reaches {max_c} degrees, with exact amounts in grams and a calculator that scales any recipe to your pizza count or pan.

style.calc_link: Change the amount in the calculator
style.body_placeholder: The detailed step-by-step instructions for this style come next. Until then, use the amounts above and the timeline in the calculator.

new_york.name: New York
new_york.blurb: Foldable slice, crisp base, chewy rim. The main recipe of this guide and the best fit for a home oven.

neapolitan.name: Neapolitan
neapolitan.blurb: Soft centre and a tall, airy rim. No oil in the dough. In a home oven it is Neapolitan-style, not the real thing.

roman_tonda.name: Roman tonda
roman_tonda.blurb: Thin, crisp and light. The dough is rolled out with a rolling pin and topped lightly.

al_taglio.name: Al taglio
al_taglio.blurb: Roman tray pizza cut into squares. Very wet dough, open crumb, crisp base.

detroit.name: Detroit
detroit.blurb: Thick, airy, with a fried crisp base and cheese baked to a dark edge. Sauce goes on top.

chicago.name: Chicago deep dish
chicago.blurb: A tall pie in a deep pan. Cheese goes at the bottom, sauce on top.

warn.parchment: Check the maximum temperature printed on your baking paper (Backpapier). Common brands are rated to {max_c} degrees, below this oven. Do not let it touch the heating elements or oven walls.
warn.parchment_grill: Baking paper is not meant for the grill function. Take the paper out before you switch the grill on, or check that your paper is rated for it.
warn.oil_smoke: Extra-virgin olive oil starts to smoke at about {min_c} to {max_c} degrees. In pans and on a hot tray use refined olive oil or a neutral oil (rapeseed, sunflower). Oil mixed into the dough is fine.
warn.yeast_varies: Yeast amounts in sources vary up to {spread} times with fridge temperature and brand. Treat these amounts as a starting point and adjust after you bake.
warn.no_oil_no_sugar: Traditional Neapolitan dough has no oil and no sugar. That rule comes from secondary sources, not from the AVPN text that was read. The oil and sugar-free version is the traditional one; sugar here only helps colour at {oven_c} degrees.
warn.method_not_typical: This method is not the usual choice for this style. It still works, but check the notes.
warn.solution_exceeds_water: The yeast solution would be more than all the water in the recipe, so the yeast is weighed directly.
warn.scale_resolution: This yeast amount is small for a scale that shows whole grams. A little more or less changes the rise, so watch the dough and adjust next time.
warn.batch_too_small: This dough is too small to measure the yeast on a scale that shows whole grams. Make a bigger batch.
warn.pan_small: This pan is very small, so there is very little dough.

calc.solution_steps:
1. Dissolve {yeast} in {water} g of lukewarm water ({pct} %).
2. Stir until dissolved and use it right away; do not store it.
3. Weigh {take} g of the solution and add it with the water.
4. Throw the rest away.

calc.packet_fresh: half of a {cube} g cube of fresh yeast ({g} g)
calc.water_note: The {take} g of solution replace the same weight of water. Add {add} g of water ({temp} degrees) plus the solution.
calc.oven_line: {temp} degrees, top and bottom heat, no fan. Rack: {rack}. Preheat the {surface} for {pre} minutes.
calc.grill_line: Grill for the last {from} to {to} minutes (never more than {max} minutes in total).
